summary: A resting native harness (Claude channel, Codex app-server, omp) replicates its harness.observed state only when it changes, not on each five-minute re-stamp; a working harness and legacy reports keep their once-a-minute refresh

replay.detail: Fewer harness.observed claims are written: an unchanged state from a resting native driver stays in the host's local observation log instead of refreshing the replicated claim, unless the seat claimed or reported work after its last replicated state or another observation of the seat is newer, because readers then fold the seat as working until a newer observation replicates. Each re-stamp still replicates any usage reading that has waited out its 5-minute interval. Old claims are untouched.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: On other nodes a resting native harness's replicated state keeps the time of its last transition instead of being refreshed every few minutes. A native event is admitted only against the seat's running runtime row, so the card overlay that reads a report's age (for a runtime row stuck before running) never applies to it, and the retention policy already treats these refreshes as heartbeats nothing reads. Wake acknowledgement still sees working reports refresh. No claim kind, field, wire or CLI contract changes; a mixed-version fleet keeps working, as an older node keeps refreshing and a newer node reads its claims as before.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the normal upgrade; no migration or backfill.

recovery.detail: No data recovery is needed. Reverting restores the once-a-minute refresh from the next re-stamp; the re-stamps that stayed local remain in each host's local observation log.
